# Astro tag-release controls and recovery

This is a disabled proposal. Both the prerequisite verification job and publication job have independent false guards; any separately authorized activation must review both. Do not enable or dispatch publication without separate authorization, a verified immutable protected tag ruleset, protected `main` first-parent merge policy, and a properly protected `astro-production-release` environment. `github.ref_protected` only says some protection applies; it does not prove that tag updates/deletions or privileged bypass are prohibited. Check those controls independently. Configure the environment with required reviewers, no self-review, restricted branches/tags and no administrator bypass where supported. Configure `ASTRO_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT_READY=yes` at environment scope only, verify no repository or organization fallback exists, and protect that configuration. The sentinel is not proof that reviews remain enforced.

Configure a new direct-publish npm trusted publisher only after separate approval, while retaining the stage-only publisher. The proposed exact identity is repository `martletdesign/astro`, workflow `tag-release.yml`, environment `astro-production-release`. Ensure npm uses OIDC without a static token and verify provenance in an authorized integration rehearsal. A registry 404 cannot detect private staged-version reservations or prevent publication races; npm is the final authority. Confirm no new tag collides with historical `/theme` tags.

The proposed workflow rejects any already-published version before publishing and checks the registry again immediately before publication. It publishes only the inspected isolated tarball and creates a GitHub Release only after the registry metadata and downloaded bytes match. A successful npm publish is irreversible. If publication succeeds but verification or GitHub Release creation fails, do not rerun the publication job: it will reject the now-existing version. An authorized maintainer must independently inspect the npm package and provenance, confirm the unchanged protected tag and first-parent production commit, reproduce the same tarball, and run `RELEASE_TAG=vX.Y.Z node scripts/tag-release-cli.mjs verify-registry /absolute/path/to/reproduced.tgz`. Record the local SHA-512, registry integrity, package identity, provenance and tag SHA. Only after separate approval may the maintainer create or reconcile the GitHub Release for that existing tag. If bytes or provenance differ, stop and investigate; never republish the version or move its tag.

The recovery procedure is manual and has not exercised a real npm publication or GitHub Release in this proposal. The legacy Astro release-event direct-publish workflow is removed in this draft; the new tag workflow remains disabled. Existing core stage-only publishers remain unchanged. Any later decision to retire or reconcile the staged path requires separate review.
